items.q: Which approach finds whether any two numbers in an unsorted array of n integers add up to a target in O(n) time?
options: Sort, then use two pointers from both ends
Check every pair with two nested loops
Look up target - x in a hash set while scanning once
Binary search for target - x for each x
items.explain: A hash set gives O(1) average lookup, so one pass is enough; sorting first costs O(n log n) and nested loops cost O(n^2).

items.q: Push 4, push 7, push 2 onto a stack, then pop once. Separately, enqueue 4, 7, 2 into a queue and dequeue once. Which values come out?
items.explain: A stack is last-in first-out and a queue is first-in first-out.

items.q:
A binary tree has root 5, left child 3, right child 8; node 3 has children 1 and 4; node 8 has right child 9.
What is the in-order traversal?
items.explain: In-order visits left subtree, node, right subtree; for a binary search tree this gives sorted order.

items.q: You need the shortest path (fewest edges) from one node to another in an unweighted graph. Which traversal guarantees it?
options: Any traversal, as long as you track the parent
items.explain: BFS explores nodes in order of distance from the start, so the first time it reaches the target is via the fewest edges.

items.q:
How many ways can you climb a staircase of 5 steps if each move is 1 or 2 steps?

ways[1] = 1, ways[2] = 2
ways[n] = ways[n-1] + ways[n-2]
items.explain: The recurrence builds 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, so ways[5] = 8; storing earlier answers is the basic idea of dynamic programming.
This is the Fibonacci sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, so f(6) = 8; without memoisation it also runs in exponential time.

items.q:
What is the time complexity of this loop for input n?

i = 1
while i < n:
    i = i * 2
items.explain: i doubles each time, so it takes about log2(n) steps to reach n.

items.q:
What does this print?

def rev(s):
    out = ""
    for ch in s:
        out = ch + out
    return out

print(rev("nagar") == "nagar", rev("level") == "level")
items.explain: Prepending each character reverses the string; "nagar" reversed is "ragan" but "level" is a palindrome.

items.q: A sorted array has 1,000,000 elements. Roughly how many comparisons does binary search need in the worst case to find a value?
items.explain: Each comparison halves the search range, and 2^20 is about 1,000,000.
